titleEn: The Mixing Bowl says it’s still ‘early days’ for crop robotics but AI, M&A are driving advancement
titleZh: 作物机器人仍处早期阶段，AI与并购推动行业进步
summaryZh: The Mixing Bowl发布2026年作物机器人行业报告，追踪400家企业，较2024年增长25%，但行业洗牌剧烈。欧洲占半数企业，美国以加州为核心。除草和喷洒领域商业化进展最快，大型农机厂商通过并购和合作积极布局。采收仍是最难攻克的领域。AI技术加速系统开发，但劳动力短缺和成本压力才是核心驱动力。
featuredReason: 虽然本文聚焦种植业作物机器人，但其对农业机器人行业格局、并购趋势、AI技术驱动力的分析，对智慧畜牧行业从业者理解农业自动化整体趋势、投资风向和技术演进路径具有重要参考价值。
contentFull:
It’s still early days for the “robotic revolution” in agriculture, according to agrifood innovation hub The Mixing Bowl and its latest Crop Robotics landscape report.

Originally launched in 2022, the landscape tracks such companies, this year across across 15 segments including weeding, harvesting, tractors, autonomy, and scouting, to name a few. (The landscape does not include nursery or post-harvest segments.)

The 2026 Crop Robotic landscape includes 400 companies, a 25% increase from 2024. Those numbers come with a caveat, however, said Chris Taylor, a partner at the Mixing Bowl. “There’s some churn in that 20% of the companies are no longer there that were there before, and more than a third on [the most recent] landscape are actually new to the landscape.”

This indicates a dynamic and active innovation environment, but also one that is extremely competitive and often difficult, he adds.

Europe as a region accounts for half the companies in the landscape, while the US leads on individual countries, representing 18% of total companies. More than 40% of those US companies are based in California. 

Investments, while nowhere near the peak of 2021, have remained steady. According to the report, companies included have collectively raised $600 million, from early seed rounds to raises north of $100 million.

The 2026 Crop Robotics Landscape. Source: The Mixing Bowl
What’s tracking

Spraying and weeding continue to see steady growth and, as Taylor points out, are some of the most popular areas for venture investing.

“We’ve seen a lot of great commercialization there,” noted Western Growers’ Ben Palone, speaking at the recent launch event for the Crop Robotic landscape.

“Quite honestly, I’m happy where we are in the commercialization stage with weeding. We’re getting [further] into the adoption phase, but now we’re seeing some market competition between companies, and it’s actually shaken up a little bit of the business models at a few of those companies.”

Elsewhere, major equipment manufacturers — think Yamaha, Deere, Caterpillar, and Kubota — have acquired companies or assets, or struck partnerships with robotics startups to bolster their own portfolios.

For example, Kubota led an investment into precision sprayer Kilter earlier this year, while Deere in 2025 acquired GUSS, maker of semi-autonomous sprayers. Deere also has an exclusive, $10 million partnership with ag robotics incubator Reservoir, among the company’s many other startup-related activities.

“There’s no question that the OEMs see that there is a future in this,” says Taylor. “How they’re getting there, whether it’s M&A of full companies or acquisitions of technology or partnering, there are different paths they’re taking but they’re all heading in that direction.”

Elsewhere, some of the better-funded startups are absorbing their peers, such as Bonsai Robotics scooping up Farm-ng and FarmX buying AMOS power.

“These M&A activities are not signs of a maturing market so much as an early-stage market concentrating its capital and talent,” notes Taylor.

What’s still challenging 

As it has been for years, harvest is still one of the most challenging categories in terms of both technical capabilities and scaling.

“It’s the hardest area in crop robotics, and it continues to lag the others. But remains the holy grail of what’s trying to be accomplished,” says Taylor.

From a purely technical standpoint, machines must ideally be able to identify the crop properly, find it in the plant canopy, then pick it without damaging the fruit or vegetable.

“You have to bring together so much technology to make that happen,” explains Taylor. Oftentimes, it has to be very crop specific as well.

Even with challenges, there are plenty of external elements driving momentum in crop robotics, not the least of which are labor shortages, increasing input costs, and a changing regulatory environment around crop protection tools.

Certain technologies, such as AI tools, play a big role in growing and scaling robotics offerings, though Taylor is quick to point out that “modern machine learning predates the current AI moment by a decade, and computer-vision models have been trained to tell a weed from a crop for some time.”

The bigger changes involving AI will be in “advancements in the underlying technologies” that allow systems to be developed faster, faster application across farm environments, and machines that are “less reactive and more predictive,” says Taylor.

“Crop robotics will continue to be a beneficiary as well as a driver of that advancement.”

translationZh:
据农业食品创新中心The Mixing Bowl及其最新作物机器人行业报告显示，农业领域的"机器人革命"仍处于早期阶段。

该行业图谱最初于2022年推出，今年追踪了15个细分领域的相关企业，包括除草、采收、拖拉机、自主导航和田间侦察等。（该图谱不包括苗圃或采后环节。）

2026年作物机器人图谱收录了400家企业，较2024年增长25%。然而，The Mixing Bowl合伙人Chris Taylor指出，这些数字需要附加说明："其中有20%的企业已经不在图谱上了，存在一定的淘汰率，而最新图谱上超过三分之一的企业实际上是新入榜的。"

他补充说，这表明了一个充满活力和活跃的创新环境，但同时也是一个竞争极其激烈且往往充满困难的环境。

从地区来看，欧洲占图谱中企业总数的一半，而美国在单个国家中领先，占总数的18%。这些美国企业中超过40%位于加利福尼亚州。

投资方面，虽然远未达到2021年的峰值，但一直保持稳定。根据报告，图谱收录的企业已累计融资6亿美元，涵盖从早期种子轮到超过1亿美元的大额融资。

**趋势追踪**

喷洒和除草领域持续稳步增长，正如Taylor所指出的，这也是风险投资最热门的领域之一。

"我们在那里看到了很多出色的商业化成果，"Western Growers的Ben Palone在最近的作物机器人图谱发布会上表示。

"说实话，我对除草领域的商业化阶段感到满意。我们正在进一步进入采用阶段，但现在我们看到企业之间出现了一些市场竞争，这实际上对其中一些企业的商业模式产生了一定冲击。"

在其他方面，大型设备制造商——如雅马哈、约翰迪尔、卡特彼勒和久保田——已经收购了企业或资产，或与机器人初创公司建立合作关系，以充实自身的产品组合。

例如，久保田今年领投了精准喷洒企业Kilter，而约翰迪尔在2025年收购了半自主喷洒机制造商GUSS。约翰迪尔还与农业机器人孵化器Reservoir建立了1000万美元的独家合作关系，这只是该公司众多与初创企业相关活动中的一部分。

"毫无疑问，原始设备制造商看到了这个领域的未来，"Taylor说。"他们如何实现这一目标——无论是整体并购企业、收购技术还是建立合作——他们走着不同的路径，但都在朝着同一个方向前进。"

此外，一些资金较为充裕的初创公司正在吸收同行，例如Bonsai Robotics收购了Farm-ng，FarmX收购了AMOS Power。

"这些并购活动与其说是市场成熟的标志，不如说是早期市场在集中资本和人才，"Taylor指出。

**仍面临的挑战**

多年来，采收在技术能力和规模化方面仍然是最具挑战性的类别之一。

"这是作物机器人中最难的领域，并且持续落后于其他领域。但它仍然是人们试图攻克的圣杯，"Taylor说。

从纯技术角度来看，机器理想情况下必须能够正确识别作物，在植物冠层中找到它，然后在不损伤果实或蔬菜的情况下进行采摘。

"你必须整合如此多的技术才能实现这一目标，"Taylor解释道。通常，这还必须针对特定作物进行定制。

尽管面临挑战，仍有大量外部因素推动着作物机器人的发展势头，尤其是劳动力短缺、投入成本上升以及围绕作物保护工具的监管环境变化。

某些技术，如AI工具，在发展和扩展机器人产品方面发挥着重要作用，不过Taylor迅速指出，"现代机器学习比当前这波AI热潮早了十年，计算机视觉模型被训练来区分杂草和作物也已经有一段时间了。"

Taylor表示，AI带来的更大变化将体现在"底层技术的进步"上，这些进步使系统能够更快地开发、更快地应用于农场环境，并使机器"更少被动反应、更多预测性。"

"作物机器人将继续成为这一进步的受益者，同时也是推动者。"
author: Jennifer Marston
